diagram_math_checks.details: Nine vertices: v,a1,b1,c1,d1,a2,b2,c2,d2. For each i=1,2 the five lobe edges are ai-ci,ai-di,bi-ci,bi-di,ci-di, and the two attaching edges are v-ai,v-bi: fourteen edges total. No ai-bi edge and no edge joins opposite lobes. Intersections of crossing lobe edges have no node, so are not extra vertices. The final standalone native figure shows all fourteen intended segments; no --cycle paths are used.

Each ai and bi has two internal neighbours ci,di plus v: degree 3. Each ci and di has the other three lobe vertices as neighbours: degree 3. Vertex v has a1,b1,a2,b2: degree 4. Sum of degrees is 8*3+4=28=2*14; minimum degree is exactly 3, agreeing with local step 1.2 and F2.

Deleting v leaves exactly two connected K4-minus-one-edge lobes, each containing ci-di and both ai,bi adjacent to ci,di. The original graph is connected. Thus the violet singleton {v} is a vertex cut and kappa=1 under F1/local definition, as in step 1.1.

diagram_math_checks.check: Edge cut and exact edge connectivity
diagram_math_checks.details: The two orange edges va1,vb1 are the entire boundary of the first lobe, so removing both disconnects it (step 1.3). For each i, va_i,vb_i lie on v-ai-ci-bi-v; ai-ci,ai-di,ci-di lie on ai-ci-di-ai; bi-ci,bi-di,ci-di lie on bi-ci-di-bi. Every edge therefore has an alternate path when deleted, and no single edge is a cut (step 1.4). Thus lambda=2.
